meta.title: JJ's ERP User Guide
meta.subtitle: Orders, kitchen, money and reports — step by step

intro.text: This guide shows you how to run JJ's deli shop with JJ's ERP, one task at a time. Each task says what it is for, then gives numbered steps with a picture of the real screen. The letters on the pictures match the letters in the steps.

cards.title: New to the system?
cards.text: Start with **Getting started**: open the shop, sign in and learn the main screen.

cards.title: Working at the counter or in the kitchen?
cards.text: **Daily work** covers orders, clients, production, the fridge, expenses and closing the day.

cards.title: Running the shop?
cards.text: **Managing the shop** covers the menu, purchases, distribution, staff, users and settings.

cards.title: The owner
cards.text: **For the owner** explains the five daily answers, reports, costs and the audit log.

parts.title: Getting started
parts.intro: Everyone reads this part first. It takes about ten minutes.

chapters.title: Open the shop and sign in
chapters.intro: JJ's ERP works with no internet. It has two parts on the shop computer: **JJ's ERP Server** keeps the data, and **JJ's ERP** is the window you work in.

tasks.title: Start the shop in the morning
tasks.goal: Do this once when you turn on the shop computer.
steps: On the desktop, double-click **JJ's ERP Server**. Nothing opens; a small JJ's icon appears next to the clock at the bottom of the screen. This means the shop is running.
Double-click **JJ's ERP** on the desktop. The work window opens.

steps.text: If you open **JJ's ERP** first, it shows *Starting the shop…* and starts the server for you. Wait a few seconds.
steps.tip: Right-click the JJ's icon next to the clock and tick **Start with Windows**. The shop then starts by itself every time the computer is turned on.

tasks.result: The sign-in screen of JJ's ERP is open.
tasks.warning: Closing the **JJ's ERP** window does not stop the shop. To really stop it, right-click the JJ's icon next to the clock and choose **Stop the shop**. Nobody can work until it is started again.

tasks.title: Sign in
tasks.goal: Each person signs in with their own username, so the system knows who did what.
before: Your username and password (the owner gives them to you)

steps.text: Type your username in [[user]].

steps: Type your password in **Password**.
Press **Log in**, or press `Enter`.
tasks.result: Your home screen opens with your name at the top.
tasks.note: The owner and managers see the full menu on the side. Members see a simpler screen with big buttons (see *What a Member sees*).

tasks.title: Learn the main screen
tasks.goal: Know where everything is before you start.

steps.text: Look at the main screen. These are its parts:

callouts.label: **The menu** — every area of the system. Click a name to open it.
**عربي / EN** — switch the language. The whole screen turns right-to-left in Arabic.
Today's dollar rate, used for SYP prices
Your name — click it to change your password or log out
**Your day in five answers** — today's sales, costs, profit and cash at a glance
**+ New order** — the fastest way to sell

steps: Click **Home** in the menu at any time to come back here.
tasks.tip: Dropdown lists and date fields work the same everywhere: click to open, click a choice. Long lists have a search box at the top — type a few letters to find an item fast.

tasks.title: Change your password or log out
tasks.goal: Change the password the owner gave you, and log out when you leave the counter.

steps.text: Click your name at the top. Choose [[pwd]] **Change password**.

callouts.label: **Log out** — use it when someone else takes the computer

steps.text: Type your current password in [[cur]], then your new password in [[new]].

steps: Press **Save**. A message *Password changed* appears.
tasks.result: Next time, sign in with the new password.
tasks.note: Forgot your password? Ask the owner. They can set a new one in **Users** → **Edit**.

tasks.title: What a Member sees
tasks.goal: Members (counter and kitchen staff) get big buttons for their daily work and never see costs or profit.

steps.text: After signing in, a Member sees this screen:

callouts.label: **New invoice** — sell to a shop or a client
The Member's menu: Orders, Production, Warehouse & fridge, Distribution

steps: Every task in **Daily work** works the same way for a Member: the screens are the same, only the menu is shorter.

parts.title: Daily work
parts.intro: Everything done at the counter and in the kitchen, many times a day.

chapters.title: Orders and invoices
chapters.intro: Every sale is an order. A new order has three steps: **1 Who** → **2 Items** → **3 Pay**.

tasks.title: Sell to a walk-in customer
tasks.goal: Use this when someone buys at the counter and pays now.

steps.text: Click **+ New order** on the home screen, or **Orders** → **+ New order**. In step 1, press [[walkin]] **Walk-in**.

callouts.label: **Walk-in** — a customer who is not registered
**Account client** — a registered shop or person
**Free trial** — free samples for a new client
**Staff purchase** — an employee buys with the staff discount
**Tasting / internal** — no payment, the cost is recorded

steps.text: Click a product to add it. If it has extras, a small window opens: choose the extras in [[extras]], set the quantity with [[qty]], then press [[add]] **Add to order**.

callouts.label: Extras like **Double filling** — each adds to the price

steps.text: Add the other products. The order builds up on [[cart]]. Then press [[next]] **Next: payment**.
sub: Click a product again to add one more, or use **+** and **−** in the order list.
Have a barcode scanner? Scan the product code into and press `Enter`.

callouts.label: Scan a barcode or type a product code
A product — the number shows how many are in the order

steps.text: Choose [[pickup]] **Pickup** and how the customer paid in [[method]]: **Cash** or **Sham Cash**.
sub: The customer pays only part? Type what they paid in **Paid now**. Leave it empty when they pay all of it.
A discount? Type the percent in **Manual discount %**.

callouts.label: Tick to print the receipt by itself every time

steps.text: Press **Confirm order**. Then press [[receipt]] **Print receipt**.

callouts.label: **Print receipt** — small receipt printer (58 or 80 mm)

tasks.result: The screen shows *Order saved* with the order number. The money is in the cash box and the products are taken from the fridge (oldest first).
tasks.tip: In **3 Pay**, tick *Print the receipt automatically* once. From then on the receipt prints as soon as you confirm.

tasks.title: Sell to a client on their account (part paid)
tasks.goal: Use this for registered shops and clients — for example an invoice of $8.50 where they pay $5 now and the rest later.

steps.text: **+ New order** → **Account client**. Find the client with [[search]] (name or phone) and click [[client]].
sub: Client not in the list? Press **+ New client**, fill the name and phone and press **Save & choose**.

callouts.label: A client — their balance shows under the name

steps: Add the products, then press **Next: payment**. The client's own prices are used by themselves.

steps.text: Choose how they paid and type what they paid now in [[paid]]. The rest goes on their account. To put the whole order on the account, choose [[credit]] **On credit**.

callouts.label: The client's balance and credit limit

steps: Press **Confirm order** and print the receipt. It shows what was paid, what is left, and the balance before and after.
tasks.result: The client's balance goes up by the unpaid part. You see it in **Clients**.
tasks.warning: If the order goes over the client's credit limit, a warning appears. When the limit is set to block, the order is refused — take a payment first (see *Take a payment from a client*).

tasks.title: Send an order with the delivery person
tasks.goal: Use this when the order goes out with Ahmad or another delivery person.
steps: Make the order as usual. In **3 Pay**, press **Delivery**.

steps.text: Type the delivery fee if there is one, and choose who delivers it in **Delivered by**.

steps: Press **Confirm order** and print the receipt for the delivery person.
When the order arrives, open it in **Orders** and press **Mark delivered**.
tasks.result: The cash stays with the delivery person until they hand it over at **Daily close**.
tasks.note: The home screen shows *Cash not handed over yet* while a delivery person still holds money.

tasks.title: Find an order and print the receipt again
tasks.goal: Use this when a customer asks for a copy of their receipt, or to check an order.

steps.text: Click **Orders** in the menu. Today's orders are shown. To see another day, click the date [[date]] and pick a day in the calendar.

callouts.label: The day — click for the calendar
Search by order number or client
An order — click it to open

steps.text: Click the order. Press [[print]] **Print receipt**, or [[a4]] **A4** for a full-page invoice.

tasks.title: Cancel an order entered by mistake
tasks.goal: Use this when an order was entered wrong. Cancel it, then make it again correctly.
steps: Open **Orders** and click the order.
Press **Cancel order** and confirm.
Make the order again the right way.
tasks.result: The order shows as cancelled. Its stock, money and client debt go back as they were.
tasks.warning: A closed day cannot be changed. If the day is already closed, only the owner (Admin) can reopen it in **Daily close**.

tasks.title: Free trial, staff purchase or tasting
tasks.goal: The other three kinds of order in step **1 Who**.
steps: **Free trial**: choose or add the prospect. Everything is free; the system remembers it so you can see later who became a client.
**Staff purchase**: choose the employee. Their staff discount is applied; they can pay or have it deducted from their salary.
**Tasting / internal**: no invoice and no payment. The goods leave stock and their cost is recorded.

chapters.title: Clients
chapters.intro: Each client has a balance: orders on credit add to what they owe, payments take it down.

tasks.title: Add a new client
tasks.goal: Register a shop or a person who buys regularly.

steps.text: Click **Clients** in the menu, then [[new]] **+ New client**.

callouts.label: Filters — for example **Owe money** or **Late payers**
A client — click to open their page

steps.text: Choose [[type]] **Business** or **Person**, and fill [[name]] and [[phone]].
sub: **Payment terms (days)** — how many days they have to pay.
**Credit limit ($)** — the most they may owe. 0 means no limit.

steps: Press **Save**.
tasks.result: The client appears in the list and can be chosen in a new order.

tasks.title: Take a payment from a client
tasks.goal: Use this when a client pays money towards what they owe.

steps.text: Open **Clients** and click the client. Their balance [[balance]] shows what they owe. Press [[pay]] **Record payment**.

callouts.label: **Balance** — red means the client owes money

steps.text: Type the amount in [[amount]], check the currency [[cur]] and choose how they paid [[method]].
sub: **This money is**: **Paying their debt**, or **Prepaid top-up** when they pay in advance.

steps: Press **Record payment**.
tasks.result: The balance goes down by the amount and the money is added to the cash box.
tasks.tip: To give the client a copy of their account, open the **Statement** tab and print it.

chapters.title: Production and the fridge
chapters.intro: In the morning you make the day's products. Each product made becomes a dated batch in the fridge with its own label.

tasks.title: Make the morning production
tasks.goal: Record what the kitchen makes today, so stock and costs stay right.

steps.text: Click **Production** in the menu. For each product, type how many you are making in [[qty]] or use **+**.

callouts.label: **Materials needed** — what this uses and what is in stock

steps: Check **Materials needed**. If a material is short, it is shown before you confirm.
Choose who made it in **Made by** and where it goes in **Put in**.
Press **Confirm production**, then **Print all labels** and stick a label on each pack.
tasks.result: The materials leave the store and the products appear in **Warehouse & fridge** with their expiry date.
tasks.note: When you sell, the system takes from the oldest batch in the fridge first.

tasks.title: Check a batch, print labels, move or count it
tasks.goal: See what is in the fridge, when it expires, and work with one batch.

steps.text: Click **Warehouse & fridge**. Scan a label into [[scan]], or click a batch [[batch]].

callouts.label: Scan a label or type a batch number
A batch — how many are left and when it expires

steps.text: Choose what to do:
sub: **Print labels** — print more labels for this batch.
**Move** — put it in another fridge or shelf.
**Count** — fix the quantity after counting.
**Who got this batch?** — every shop that received it.

tasks.title: Record waste
tasks.goal: Use this when products expire, fall or are thrown away. It keeps stock and profit honest.
steps: Open the batch in **Warehouse & fridge** and press **Waste**.

steps.text: Type how many in [[qty]] and choose the reason in [[reason]].

steps: Press **Record waste**.
tasks.result: The quantity leaves the fridge and appears in the waste report.

tasks.title: Record an expense
tasks.goal: Every time the shop spends money — gas, repairs, cleaning — record it so the profit is right.

steps.text: Click **Expenses**, then **+ Add expense**. Choose what it was for in [[item]].
sub: Not in the list? The last choice, **+ Add new**, adds it to the list.

steps: Type the amount in **Amount**.

steps.text: Choose the cash box in **Paid from**. The list opens; the chosen box has a check mark.

callouts.label: Click the box the money came from

steps.text: The date is today. For another day, click **Date** and pick the day in the calendar.

callouts.label: Click the month to jump to another month

steps: Press **Save expense**.
tasks.result: The expense is in the list and the money is taken from the cash box.
tasks.tip: Rent or a bill not paid yet? Choose **Not paid yet** at the top of the form and set the **Due date**. It waits in **Due (not paid)** until you pay it.

tasks.title: Close the day
tasks.goal: At the end of the day: take the cash from the delivery person, count the cash box and lock the day.

steps.text: Click **Daily close**. In *1 · Settle with the delivery person*, take the cash and press [[rep]] **Cash received**.

callouts.label: **Cash received** — the delivery person handed over the money
**Counted** — the cash you counted in the box
**Personal withdrawal** — money the owner takes out

steps: Count all the cash in the box. Type the total in **Counted**. The system shows what should be in the box and the difference.

steps.text: If everything is right, press [[lock]] **Close the day**.

steps: Print the day report if you want a paper copy.
tasks.result: The day is locked. No orders or money moves can be added to it.
tasks.warning: Only the owner (Admin) can reopen a closed day, with **Reopen**. Check the count before you close.
tasks.note: A personal withdrawal lowers the cash box but not the profit. It has its own report.

parts.title: Managing the shop
parts.intro: Setting up the menu, buying stock, distribution, staff and the system settings.

tasks.title: Add or change a product and its recipe
tasks.goal: Keep the menu, prices and recipes right — the recipe is what makes costs and stock correct.

steps.text: Click **Menu**. Press [[new]] **+ Product**, or click a product [[row]] to change it.

callouts.label: **Margin** — profit as a percent of the price

steps.text: Choose the category [[cat]], and type the names and the price [[price]].
sub: **Shelf life (hours)** sets the expiry date on the labels.
Lower down, the recipe lists each ingredient and packaging with its quantity. The cost per piece updates as you type.

callouts.label: Cost of one piece from the recipe

steps: Press **Save** at the bottom of the window.
tasks.result: The product appears in new orders with the new price. Old invoices keep their old price.

tasks.title: Enter a supplier's invoice
tasks.goal: When goods arrive from a supplier, enter the invoice so stock, costs and supplier debts are right.

steps.text: Click **Purchasing** → **New purchase**. Choose the supplier [[supplier]] and type their invoice number [[inv]].

steps: Add a line for each item: the item, quantity, unit price, where it goes and the expiry date.
Fill the discount and transport if any — they are spread over the items' real cost.
Type what you paid now. If you pay later, set the due date.
Press **Save purchase**.
tasks.result: The items are in stock at their real cost. Anything unpaid shows in **Supplier debts**.
tasks.note: If a price went up, **Costing** → **Price changes** shows which products lost margin.

tasks.title: Route sheet, consignment and returns
tasks.goal: For shops the delivery person visits: what to deliver, goods left on consignment, and goods coming back.

steps.text: Click **Distribution**. Choose the day and the delivery person, then press [[print]] **Print route sheet** for the driver.

callouts.label: **Consignment** — leave goods, they pay only for what they sell

steps: For each shop: **Invoice** to sell, **Consignment** to leave goods, or **Return** when goods come back.
On a return, choose for each line: back to the fridge, or waste. Then choose whether the client is credited or refunded.
tasks.note: To settle a consignment: open the **Consignment** tab, count what came back, and the sold part becomes an invoice at the agreed price.

tasks.title: Employees, advances and payroll
tasks.goal: Keep each employee's pay, record advances (سلف) and run the monthly payroll.

steps.text: Click **People & payroll**. Press [[new]] **+ Employee** to add someone, and choose how they are paid: fixed, commission, or both.

steps: When an employee takes money in advance, record it in the **Advances** tab.

At the end of the month, open **Payroll** and pick the **Month**. Check each person's **Net pay**, choose the box in **Pay from box** and press **Pay salaries**. Advances and staff purchases are taken from the salary.

tasks.title: Add a user and choose their role
tasks.goal: Give each person their own sign-in. The role decides what they can see and do.

steps.text: Click **Users** → [[new]] **New user**.

callouts.label: A user — **Edit** to change the name, role or password

steps.text: Fill the name [[name]], username [[user]] and password [[pass]]. Choose the role [[role]] and language [[lang]].

steps: Press **Save** and give the person their username and password.
tasks.result: The person can sign in now.
tasks.warning: When someone leaves, press **Deactivate** — don't share passwords. The last Admin cannot be deactivated.

tasks.title: Change what a role can do
tasks.goal: Decide exactly which areas each role can view, add, edit, delete or export.

steps.text: Click **Roles & permissions** and choose a role [[list]].

callouts.label: Tick what this role may do in each area
**See costs** — without it, the user gets the simple screens

steps: Tick or untick the boxes in the grid, then press **Save**.
tasks.note: The Admin role always keeps every permission. You can add your own role with **New role**.

tasks.title: Set the dollar rate
tasks.goal: Prices are in dollars; the rate turns them into Syrian pounds. Set it before selling in SYP.

steps.text: Click **Settings** → **Currency & rate**. Type today's rate in [[manual]] (1 USD = how many SYP).

callouts.label: A rate website, used when there is internet (optional)

steps: Press **Use this rate**.
tasks.result: The rate shows at the top of every screen. Old orders keep the rate of their day, so reports never change.

tasks.title: Back up and restore the data
tasks.goal: The system copies all data once a day by itself and keeps the last 30 copies. You can also make a copy now or go back to an old one.

steps.text: Click **Settings** → **Backups**. Press [[now]] **Back up now** before big changes.

steps: To go back to a copy, press **Restore** next to it and confirm.
Stop the shop (right-click the JJ's icon → **Stop the shop**) and start it again. The copy is applied when it starts.
tasks.danger: Restoring replaces today's data with the old copy. The replaced data is kept as a backup, but anything entered after that copy will not be in the system.
tasks.tip: Once a week, copy the backups folder to a USB stick and keep it at home.

parts.title: For the owner
parts.intro: How to follow the shop's money in a few minutes a day.

tasks.title: Read your day in five answers
tasks.goal: The five questions every owner asks at the end of the day, answered on the home screen.

steps.text: Open **Home**. Read the five boxes from first to last:
sub: **1. How much did I really sell?** — sales after discounts.
**2. What did the goods I sold cost me?** — ingredients and packaging.
**3. What did I earn after all expenses?** — profit after today's expenses.
**4. How much cash do I have, and what do shops owe me?**
**5. Are my prices still profitable?** — *Yes* when every product is above the target margin.

callouts.label: **Send on WhatsApp** — send the five answers to your phone

steps: Press **Send on WhatsApp** to keep a copy on your phone.

tasks.title: See reports for any period
tasks.goal: Sales, profit and loss, money, products and clients for a day, a month or any dates.

steps.text: Click **Reports**. Choose a period in [[presets]] (**Today**, **This month**…) or pick dates in [[range]].
Scroll down for money, products, categories, clients and waste. Under **More reports** you find cash flow, month comparison, purchases, debts and more.

steps: Press **Print** for a paper copy. Lists can also be exported to Excel (CSV, opens with Arabic).

tasks.title: Check the cost and margin of every product
tasks.goal: Know what each sandwich really costs and the price that gives your target margin.

steps.text: Click **Costing**. The **Product costs** tab lists each product's cost, profit and [[margin]].

callouts.label: **Price for target** — the price that reaches your target margin

steps: If a margin is low, compare the price with **Price for target** and change the price in **Menu**.
tasks.tip: **Prep & forecast** shows what to prepare tomorrow from the standing orders.

tasks.title: See who did what
tasks.goal: Every change in the system is written down: who, what and when.

steps.text: Click **Audit log**. Filter by record, user or dates in [[filter]].

callouts.label: One change — press **Details** to see before and after

steps: Press **Details** on a line to see the values before and after.
tasks.note: Passwords are never shown in the log.

quick_reference.how: **+ New order** → **Account client** → client → products → **Paid now** → **Confirm order**

quick_reference.action: Add a product or change a price

faq.a: No. Everything works with no internet. The internet is only used for the automatic dollar rate and the optional cloud copy.

faq.q: I closed the JJ's ERP window. Is the shop stopped?
faq.a: No. The shop keeps running in **JJ's ERP Server** (the icon next to the clock). Open **JJ's ERP** again to continue.

faq.q: Why can't I see Reports or Costing?
faq.a: Your role doesn't allow it. Members get the simple screens. Ask the owner if you need more.

faq.q: I made a mistake in an order. What do I do?
faq.a: A manager opens the order in **Orders**, presses **Cancel order**, and you make it again. Stock, money and debt go back.

faq.q: A client wants to pay only part of an invoice.
faq.a: Make the order as an **Account client** and type what they pay in **Paid now**. The rest goes on their balance.

faq.q: How do I switch between Arabic and English?
faq.a: Press **عربي** or **EN** at the top of the screen. Each user keeps their own language.

faq.q: Can I change an order after the day is closed?
faq.a: No. Only the owner (Admin) can reopen the day in **Daily close** → **Reopen**.
On the shop computer, in `%APPDATA%\jjs-erp\data`. A copy is made every day in the `backups` folder next to it.
Ask the owner. They open **Users** → **Edit** and set a new one.

troubleshooting.problem: JJ's ERP shows *The shop is not started*
troubleshooting.cause: JJ's ERP Server is not running and could not be found.
troubleshooting.fix: Double-click **JJ's ERP Server** on the desktop, wait a few seconds.

troubleshooting.cause: A typo, Caps Lock on, or the user was deactivated.
troubleshooting.fix: Type again slowly; check Caps Lock. If it still fails, ask the owner to check **Users**.

troubleshooting.problem: A button is grey and can't be pressed
troubleshooting.cause: Something required is missing (for example no products in the order), or your role doesn't allow it.
troubleshooting.fix: Fill the missing field. If it is a permission, ask the owner.

troubleshooting.problem: *This order passes the client's credit limit and will be refused.*
troubleshooting.cause: The client owes too much and their limit blocks new credit.
troubleshooting.fix: Take a payment first (**Record payment**), or ask a manager to raise the credit limit.

troubleshooting.problem: Can't sell in SYP — the rate is missing
troubleshooting.fix: **Settings** → **Currency & rate** → type the rate → **Use this rate**.

troubleshooting.cause: The printer is off, out of paper, or the wrong paper size is set.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the printer. Set the size (58 or 80 mm) in **Settings** → **Printing**.
A manager or the owner closes it.

troubleshooting.problem: The difference at daily close is not zero
troubleshooting.cause: Cash counted wrong, a payment not entered, or an expense missing.
troubleshooting.fix: Count again. Check today's expenses and client payments, then close.

glossary.definition: A customer who is not registered and pays at the counter.
A registered shop or person with a balance; they can buy on credit.
What a client owes (red) or has paid in advance.
The most a client may owe. It can warn or block new credit.
One lot of a product made at one time, with its own number, label and expiry.
Goods left at a shop that pays only for what it sells.
Products thrown away; recorded so stock and profit stay right.
Profit as a percent of the price.
Counting the cash and locking the day so it can't be changed.
Money the owner takes from the box; it lowers the cash, not the profit.
Money an employee takes before payday; taken from the salary.
Admin, Manager or Member — decides what a user sees and does.

support.title: Need help?
support.text: Ask the shop owner first. Keep this guide next to the counter computer.
